messages.author: 3345fe7ecebfb837
messages.subject: tuning soil masking
parts:
Hello again,

I wanted to follow up with another possibility for improving my results. I've noticed that when using the default fieldMask() parameters to remove soil from my images, some leaves with a more yellow color are also being masked. I should also mention that I'm working with loamy soil that can appear very light when dry.

I've looked through the fieldMask() documentation, but am not sure what parameters would be best to modify. I also know that it may be asking a bit much of the software to differentiate between soil and yellow vegetation, but am willing to try any suggestions to see if an improvement is possible.

Thanks again,
Brian

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: tuning soil masking
parts:
Hi Brian,

 

Thanks for asking us. The best way is to choose different vegetation indices and try to find the best thresholding value to make your segmentation between plants and soil. Please, check this example using the index “BGI”: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6. Normally, plotting the histogram helps to find the best clipping point (between pics of histogram bars)

 

Image<- stack("Image.tif")

 Image.BGI<- fieldIndex(mosaic = Image, index = c("BGI"))

 dev.off()

hist(Image.BGI$BGI) # Image segmentation start from 0.7 (soil and plants)

 EX1.BGI<- fieldMask(mosaic = EX1.Rotated, Red = 1, Green = 2, Blue = 3,

                   index = "BGI", cropValue = 0.7, cropAbove = T)

 #Check if: cropValue=0.8 or cropValue=0.6 works better.




Also, there are some explanation about image segmentation in this tutorial of how to count seeds from images using FIELDimagR. Besides being different objects (seeds vs. plants) the idea to segment the background is the same You can use this to understand the concepts. Here is the link https://filipematias23.github.io/FIELDimageR-Workshop-12/#example-03


 

Hope it helps,

Filipe

messages.author: 840f9155920fe615
messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: Re: tuning soil masking
parts:
Hi Brian,

Just as another tip. Despite this empirical approach solving almost
all cases is possible to obtain a thresholding value by some criteria
decision like Otsu’s multilevel thresholding method (MOM). The
autothresholdr package does it, but index values must be discretized.
For example for an NDVI raster:

land_ndvi_F <- round(land_ndvi*100,0)

# Percentile Otsu’s multilevel thresholding method (MOM)
MOM<-auto_thresh(
int_arr=values(land_ndvi_F),
method="Percentile",
ignore_black = FALSE,
ignore_white = FALSE,
ignore_na = TRUE
)
MOM
[1] 33
or 0.33 in real NDVI data scale.

Best wishes,
Alexandre
